CFML Language Reference: Functions

Compare

Performs a case-sensitive comparison of two strings, character by character, and tells you which one sorts first.

Category

String functions

Syntax

Compare(string1, string2)

Parameters

string1
The first string.
string2
The second string.

Returns

-1 if string1 is less than string2, 0 if they are identical, 1 if string1 is greater than string2.

Usage

Characters are compared by their character codes, so all uppercase letters sort before all lowercase letters: "Zebra" comes before "apple". Use CompareNoCase to ignore case.

The EQ operator in a CFIF is case-insensitive; Compare(a, b) EQ 0 is how you test for an exact, case-sensitive match, for example when checking a password.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Pairs = "apple/apple,apple/Apple,apple/banana,Zebra/apple">
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>String 1</TH><TH>String 2</TH><TH>Compare</TH><TH>CompareNoCase</TH></TR>
<CFLOOP LIST="#Pairs#" INDEX="p">
<CFSET a = ListFirst(p, "/")><CFSET b = ListLast(p, "/")>
<CFOUTPUT><TR><TD>#a#</TD><TD>#b#</TD>
<TD ALIGN="CENTER">#Compare(a, b)#</TD><TD ALIGN="CENTER">#CompareNoCase(a, b)#</TD></TR></CFOUTPUT>
</CFLOOP>
</TABLE>

See also

CompareNoCase, Find, ListSort
